# Coefficient Stability & Sample-Size Convergence (Fig. S1) {#stability}

```{r ch7-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

Do regional differences in fitted attenuation slopes ($\alpha_{\text{NAP}}, \alpha_{\text{DOC}}, \alpha_{\text{Chl }a}$) reflect real biogeochemical differences across ecoregions, or just small-sample estimation noise?

To answer this, we randomly partition the **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_training()))`** training matchups into $G$ subsets of varying sample size ($n/50, n/100, \dots, n/10{,}000$, plus $G=1$) and refit the three-constituent model across `r P$random_reps` independent Monte Carlo replicates (`random_subset_coefs()` in `R/models.R`, seed `P$random_seed = 20240826`).

```{r figS1, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.6, fig.width = 9.2, fig.cap = 'Figure S1: Coefficient coherence cones across sample sizes. Grey ribbons span the 0.001%–99.999% quantiles of slopes fitted to random subsets of size n across all data and by water-body type. Colored circles mark Level III ecoregion fits (Models 7 and 8).'}
rand <- get_random_subsets()
m <- get_models()
c7 <- tidy_coefs(list(m7 = m$m7))
c8 <- tidy_coefs(list(m8 = m$m8))
pS1 <- figS1(cone_envelope(rand), c7, c8)
save_fig(pS1, 'figS1_coefficient_cones', 9, 5.5)
pS1
```

Once group sample size exceeds $n \approx 1{,}000$, random sampling variability narrows into a tight cone around the continental mean (`grey ribbon`). Regional estimates of $\alpha_{\text{Chl }a}$ (`chl_a`, top row) stay tightly clustered inside the random-sampling cone, whereas ecoregion-specific slopes for $\alpha_{\text{DOC}}$ (`doc`, middle row) and $\alpha_{\text{NAP}}$ (`tss_dead`, bottom row) spread well outside the random-sampling envelope even at $n > 10{,}000$. That spread reflects genuine regional differences in dissolved organic matter aromaticity (Spencer et al. 2012; Griffin et al. 2018) and suspended particle size and mineralogy (Dodds & Whiles 2004; Gohin et al. 2005).

```{r random, echo = FALSE}
rand %>% count(each_group, name = 'Total Monte Carlo coefficient estimates (3 terms × G groups × 10 reps)') %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), fmt_n)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Random Subset Sample Size (n)', 'Monte Carlo Parameter Estimates')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```
